patch_description:
This model scores the two neighbors chosen at each node jointly, rather than rewarding selected two-hop paths. A demand-biased fractional network supplies multihop continuation distances. Each possible neighbor pair is then evaluated as a two-gateway routing problem, balancing route length against unequal gateway loads.

Outgoing and incoming gateway costs capture complementary congestion risks. Their additive components become linear terms; only genuine pair interactions remain quadratic. This centering preserves rankings of valid networks while reducing unnecessary coefficient bias. The model uses at most \(n(n-1)(n-2)+n(n-1)/2\) couplings, scales its distance estimates with network size, and requires no routing solver. Improved performance remains to be verified by the evaluator.
